items.followUp: Write the SI unit of work and define it.

rubric.why: Identifies the SI unit of power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating watt or its symbol W.

rubric.why: Defines one watt in terms of work and time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one watt is one joule of work done per second, or an equivalent definition.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of power is the watt (W).
One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second: 1 W = 1 J s⁻¹.

items.followUp: Define work and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Pressure is caused by a force acting normally on a surface.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying that the force acts normally or perpendicularly on the surface.

rubric.why: Gives the defining relationship for pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining pressure as normal force per unit area, or writing its formula.

modelAnswer: Pressure is the normal force acting per unit area of a surface.
P = F/A

items.followUp: Define compressive strain and write its formula.

rubric.why: Identifies the change in length relative to the original length.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that tensile strain is the increase (or change) in length per original length.

rubric.why: Gives the ratio defining tensile strain.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct formula using extension divided by original length.

modelAnswer: Tensile strain is the ratio of the increase in length of a body to its original length when a tensile force acts on it.
Tensile strain = change in length/original length = ΔL/L

items.followUp: Use a speed-time graph to prove that v_f = v_i + at.

rubric.why: Represents initial and final velocities on a speed-time graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a speed-time graph with initial velocity v_i and final velocity v_f identified.

rubric.why: Uses the slope of the speed-time graph as acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the graph's slope with acceleration or writing the equivalent acceleration relation.

rubric.why: Forms the acceleration equation from the change in velocity over time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining a = (v_f − v_i)/t or its rearranged form.

rubric.why: Rearranges to the required result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final equation.

modelAnswer: Draw a speed-time graph with time t on the horizontal axis and speed v on the vertical axis; mark v_i at t = 0 and v_f at time t.
The slope of a speed-time graph gives acceleration: a = (v_f − v_i)/t.
Therefore, at = v_f − v_i.
Hence, v_f = v_i + at.

items.followUp: Find the centripetal force needed for a 0.4 kg body moving at 5 m s⁻¹ in a circle of radius 2 m.

rubric.why: Identifies the data in SI units, including converting the radius.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for m = 0.5 kg, r = 0.5 m, and v = 3 m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: Uses the centripetal-force formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Substitutes the given values into the formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution with units or an equivalent numerical expression.

rubric.why: Evaluates the expression correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining the numerical value 9.

rubric.why: States the force with its SI unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final answer 9 N.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 0.5 kg, r = 50 cm = 0.5 m, v = 3 m s⁻¹.
Formula: F_c = mv²/r.
Substitution: F_c = (0.5 kg)(3 m s⁻¹)²/(0.5 m).
F_c = 9 kg m s⁻².
The required centripetal force is 9 N.

items.followUp: A force of 40 N makes an angle of 60° with the x-axis. Find its perpendicular components.

rubric.why: Selects the correct horizontal-component relation for the angle shown.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using F_x = F cos 30° and F_y = F sin 30° (or equivalent).

rubric.why: Substitutes the force and angle for the x-component.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substituting 50 N and 30° into the x-component relation.

rubric.why: Calculates the horizontal component correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for F_x ≈ 43.3 N (or 25√3 N).

rubric.why: Substitutes the force and angle for the y-component.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substituting 50 N and 30° into the y-component relation.

rubric.why: Calculates the vertical component correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for F_y = 25 N.

modelAnswer: Resolve the 50 N force into perpendicular components along the x- and y-axes.
The perpendicular components are 43.3 N along the x-axis and 25 N along the y-axis.

items.followUp: Define a fundamental unit and give an example of a derived unit.

rubric.why: Indicates that derived units are formed from fundamental units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining derived units as units obtained by combining fundamental units.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of a derived unit or derived quantity with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example, such as m s⁻¹ for velocity or the newton (kg m s⁻²) for force.

modelAnswer: Derived units are units obtained by combining two or more fundamental units.
For example, the unit of velocity is metre per second (m s⁻¹).

rubric.why: States the equal-distance condition in the definition of uniform speed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that equal distances are covered.

rubric.why: States that the equal distances are covered in equal time intervals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including equal intervals of time.

modelAnswer: A body has uniform speed if it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, however small the intervals may be.
